hero.title: The native IDE for Java, Gradle and Spring.
hero.lede: Written in Rust, with its own Java engine, and TypeScript for Node projects and Playwright tests. Git is built in, Claude Code, Codex, opencode and Amp edit live in your editor and can drive the whole app, and the window can stay on your desk while the project lives on a Linux machine over SSH.
hero.proof: macOS, Linux and Windows. MIT licensed. No account, no price.
hero.shotAlt: SnoutCode on a Spring Boot web shop: the Project view, the editor and the Spring window listing the beans

features.title: An IDE that knows your build
features.sub: SnoutCode reads a Gradle or Maven build the way the build sees itself, modules, source sets, dependencies and all, and gives the editor everything that follows from it.

playwright.title: End to end tests, as a project of their own
playwright.sub: A repository of Playwright tests opens as its own kind of project and tests the application from the outside, through its URL. It gets TypeScript editing and the Node, packages and browsers it needs, and never starts Java.

ready.title: Ready to run
ready.body: A bar installs the packages with npm, pnpm, Yarn or Bun, by the lockfile, and the browsers its Playwright version runs. The output shows in the Build window.

environments.title: Environments
environments.body: Your machine, staging, a review app: each environment sets BASE_URL, its variables and a .env file. They stay outside the repository, so each tester has their own.

history.title: History
history.body: Every run is kept, the latest 200 of each project, with its environment, branch and commit, and the tests that broke since the run before.

node.title: TypeScript, on the Node your project asks for
node.sub: A package.json project opens as a Node project, without Java. Its scripts run and debug the way a Java project's do, and its editing comes from the project's own TypeScript.
node.guide: TypeScript and JavaScript in the user guide

editing.title: TypeScript editing
editing.body: Completion with auto imports, hover, go to definition, find references, rename, quick fixes and problems, from the TypeScript your project installs.

version.title: The right Node, found
version.body: From .nvmrc, .node-version, volta or engines, among the Nodes of nvm, Volta, fnm, asdf, mise and Homebrew. When none fits, it downloads one and checks it.

beside.title: Beside a Java build
beside.body: A Spring Boot application with its front end, or with an e2e folder of Playwright tests, gets each language server for its own files.

agents.title: Watch your agent type
agents.sub: Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Amp or your own agent runs in a docked console. Each edit is typed in live, with the agent's own caret and colour, and every line it wrote stays marked.

claude.how: Connects as its IDE, and its hooks report each edit.

codex.how: Hooks for the session report each edit.

opencode.how: A plugin loaded for the session reports each edit.

amp.how: A plugin of SnoutCode's reports each edit, shell writes too.

custom.name: Your own
custom.how: Any command line agent: what changes during its turn is put down to it.

setup.title: Set up for the session
setup.body: Pick an agent in the console and it starts with what it needs to report its edits; one not installed yet installs from there with a click. Codex asks you to trust its hooks once. Your own Codex and opencode settings are never changed.

ask.title: Ask it from the editor
ask.body: Send the selection, or ask the agent to fix a problem, from the code itself. The file and lines arrive in its prompt.

drives.title: It drives the window too
drives.body: Beyond its edits, the agent can open the project it made, run its tests, read what failed and show you, through SnoutCode's own API. {link}.

git.title: Git, right where you work
git.sub: Changes, diffs, commits, branches and history, in a Git view of its own. It runs the git you already have, so hooks, credentials and settings behave as they do in a terminal.

remote.title: Your window, their machine
remote.sub: Keep the window on your Mac while the project, Git, the Java engine, builds, runs, terminals and your coding agent are on a Linux machine you reach with ssh.

java.title: Java, all the way down
java.body: Completion, navigation and refactoring from SnoutCode's Java engine, on the classpath your build really has.
points: Completion that adds the import, and go to definition into libraries
Find references, rename, quick fixes and organize imports
Extract method, variable and constant
Call and type hierarchy, parameter hints, problems as you type
java.alt: Java completion in SnoutCode, suggesting members with their types

gradle.title: Gradle and Maven, as they are
gradle.body: Open a folder with one build or many side by side. The Project view shows the modules as the build sees them.
points: Multi-project and composite builds, buildSrc, the Kotlin DSL, version catalogs
Maven reactors, parent POMs, BOM imports and profiles, with no Maven install
A JDK that suits each build, offered as a download when none is installed
Gradle 7.0 to 9.x, Maven 3.6 to 3.9, JDK 17, 21 and 25

spring.title: Spring, as Spring sees it
spring.body: Beans, where each one is injected, and the endpoints of a Spring Boot application, all in one window.

Endpoints by path and method, a click from their handler
Active profiles, evaluated by the engine
Completion and checks in application.properties and application.yml

run.title: Run, test and debug
run.body: Run configurations and gutter run icons, tests in a tree with their results, and a debugger that shows values inline.

Evaluate any expression while stopped
Rerun the failed tests, from the gutter or the Tests window

pwWrite.body: Act in the browser and the steps are written into your spec as you go, right where the caret is.
points: Record at Cursor: into the test the caret is in, as a new test, or as a whole spec
Pick Locator: each element you click puts its locator at the caret

Playwright's UI Mode and Inspector a click away

pwRun.title: Follow every run, test by test
pwRun.body: Run all, a project, a file or the test at the caret, and watch the Tests window fill in as the run goes.
points: Progress, time left, each worker's step, a grid of tests by browser
The last ten results of every test and its flaky rate

Rerun failed, from the Tests window, the title bar or the gutter

Follow the agent from file to file, or keep your own place

git.title: From change to push

open.title: Free, open, and yours to change

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
intro: This Privacy Policy explains what happens to your information when you use SnoutCode, the free and open source desktop IDE published by SnoutData Inc., an Ontario corporation ("SnoutData", "we", "us", or "our"), and its website at snoutcode.com. It covers only SnoutCode and snoutcode.com, and no other SnoutData product or website.

short.title: The short version
points: SnoutCode has no account and no sign in.
It has no telemetry, no analytics and no crash reporting. It does not send us your code, your projects, your settings or your logs.
Your projects and settings stay on your computer, or on a machine of your own when you use Remote SSH.
The connections it does make are listed below: update checks to GitHub, the downloads a build needs, the Git remotes you use, and the coding agent you choose, if you choose one.
The website sets no cookies and has no analytics or tracking.

local.title: What stays on your computer
body: SnoutCode works on the files on your computer. Your projects and their contents stay there. SnoutData has no copy of them and no way to see them.
SnoutCode keeps its own files in these folders, on your computer only:
points: macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/SnoutCode` for settings and data, `~/Library/Caches/SnoutCode` for caches, and `~/Library/Logs/SnoutCode` for logs.

Linux: `~/.config/SnoutCode` for settings, `~/.local/share/SnoutCode` for data, `~/.cache/SnoutCode` for caches, and `~/.local/state/SnoutCode` for logs and history, or the folders your XDG variables name.
Windows: `%APPDATA%\SnoutCode` for settings, and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\SnoutCode` for data, caches and logs.
after: They hold your settings, your recent projects and SSH hosts, window layouts, the record of what coding agents changed in a project (with the first line of the prompt behind each change), logs, and the JDKs and other tools SnoutCode downloaded. To remove them, delete these folders. We cannot do that for you, because we do not have them.

telemetry.title: No telemetry
body: SnoutCode does not collect usage data, does not report crashes or errors to us, and does not give your installation an identifier. Its logs stay on your computer. It is open source, so you can check this in {source}.
We do not sell personal data, and SnoutCode sends us none.

updates.title: Installing and updating SnoutCode
body: Official builds are published on GitHub, and the website's download page links to them. If you install SnoutCode from the Microsoft Store, Microsoft handles that download and your use of the Store under its own terms and privacy statement.

About 30 seconds after it starts, and every 4 hours while it stays open, an installed copy of SnoutCode asks GitHub whether a newer release exists. On macOS and Windows, when SnoutCode can replace itself, it then downloads the newer version from GitHub in the background. Otherwise, as on Linux, it only tells you that one is out.

These are ordinary requests for public files. They carry no identifier and nothing about you or your projects. As with any web request, GitHub sees your IP address, and the file downloaded shows your operating system and processor type. GitHub handles these requests under its own privacy policy. It also keeps a public count of how many times each release file has been downloaded, which does not say who downloaded it.
To stop automatic checks, turn off Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Updates ▸ Check for updates automatically. A build you make from source never checks.

downloads.title: Downloads a build needs
body: SnoutCode gets some tools from their publishers. Each request says which version it needs and for which system. It carries nothing about you or your project, though as with any web request the publisher sees your IP address and handles the request under its own privacy policy.
points: Java: when a project needs a JDK you do not have, SnoutCode offers to download Eclipse Temurin. If you accept, it asks the Adoptium service (api.adoptium.net) and downloads the JDK from the address Adoptium gives.
Maven: for a Maven project with no wrapper, SnoutCode downloads Apache Maven from Maven Central (repo.maven.apache.org) the first time it needs it.
Node: when a project needs a version of Node you do not have, SnoutCode offers to download it from nodejs.org.
JavaScript debugger: the first time you debug a Node or Playwright project, SnoutCode downloads Microsoft's js-debug from its GitHub releases.

dependencies.title: Your project's dependencies
body: Building a project runs that project's own tools, such as Gradle, Maven, npm, pnpm, Yarn or Bun. They download what the project declares from the repositories it or your settings name, such as Maven Central or the npm registry. Playwright downloads its browsers when you choose Install browsers. Those servers are chosen by your project and those tools, not by SnoutCode, and each is run under its operator's own terms and privacy policy.

spring.title: New Spring Boot projects
body: When you choose Spring Boot in the New Project wizard, SnoutCode asks the Spring Initializr service (start.spring.io) which versions and dependencies it offers. When you create the project, what you entered is sent to that service so that it can generate the project: the name, group, artifact, package name, Java version, build tool, Spring Boot version and the dependencies you picked. Spring Initializr is a third party service under its own terms and privacy policy.

git.title: Git and your remote repositories
body: SnoutCode uses Git on your computer. Cloning, fetching, pulling and pushing connect to the remote repositories you set up, such as GitHub or a server of your own, with your own Git credentials. To show what there is to pull, SnoutCode also fetches the repositories in its list in the background, every 10 minutes by default. You can change the interval in Settings ▸ Version Control ▸ Fetch every. None of this passes through SnoutData.

agents.title: Third party coding agents
body: SnoutCode can run a coding agent in its console: Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Amp, or a command line agent of your own. Agents are optional and do not ship with SnoutCode. You install each one separately (when you ask, SnoutCode can run the agent's own installer for you) and you sign in to it with its provider.

An agent is a separate program, under its own provider's terms and privacy policy. What it reads in your project and what you ask it may be sent to its provider's service. SnoutCode does not control that, and none of it goes to SnoutData.

SnoutCode talks to agents only on the machine they run on, over the loopback interface (127.0.0.1), to follow their edits and, for an agent connected to the editor, to show it your selection and open files. With Remote SSH, that connection travels over your SSH connection.

remote.title: Remote SSH
body: With Remote SSH, SnoutCode uses your system's `ssh` to connect to a Linux machine you choose. Your project, Git, the Java engine, builds and terminals run on that machine, and what SnoutCode shows you travels over that SSH connection, between your computer and your machine. None of it passes through SnoutData.

SnoutCode installs a small server and the files it needs on that machine, under `~/.snout-code` and `~/.cache/SnoutCode`. When Java is needed there, the machine downloads Eclipse Temurin itself, or, if it cannot reach the internet, your computer downloads it and copies it over. Passwords and passphrases you type go to `ssh`, and SnoutCode does not store them. The list of recent hosts stays on your computer.

website.title: The website
body: snoutcode.com is a static site with no backend. It sets no cookies, has no analytics, advertising or tracking tags, and loads no scripts or fonts from other sites.
If you choose a language or a theme, that choice is kept in your browser's local storage, under `lang` and `theme`. It stays in your browser and is not sent to us.

The site is hosted on Cloudflare Pages, and Cloudflare also provides its DNS. Like any host, Cloudflare processes the technical data needed to deliver and protect the site, such as IP addresses and request details, under its own privacy policy. Cloudflare's response headers also ask browsers that support it to report failed connections to Cloudflare (Network Error Logging).
Download and source links lead to GitHub, which has its own terms and privacy policy.

messages.title: If you write to us
body: If you email {email}, we receive your address and your message, and we use them to answer you. If you open an issue on GitHub, it is public there, under GitHub's terms.

choices.title: Your choices
body: SnoutCode has no account and sends us nothing, so there is nothing about your use of it for us to look up, correct or delete. You control its data yourself: delete the folders above, and turn off update checks if you prefer.
For a question about this policy, or about a message you sent us, write to {email}.
